citations.title: Reconstruction and uncertainty
citations.relevance_note: RTS Kalman smoothing estimates missing daily thermal measurements using a state model, other available sensors and a historical cross-sensor prior. A reconstructed value is an estimate, not a direct observation or proof of a continuing fire. A 95 percent model interval describes uncertainty of the modeled state; it is not the probability that a named fire occurred. Partially reconstructed days can also contain real observations.

citations.title: Visible map versus regional energy estimate
citations.relevance_note: Both map and regional totals fuse available sensors within each H3 cell and integrate against its exact area. The visible map contains observed energy only. The temporal regional estimate may also reconstruct explicitly evidenced observation gaps; unknown days are not silently filled. With reconstruction disabled the same period and filters give the same energy. The data are a one-hour integration proxy from sparse satellite samples, not continuous measured heat release. Biomass is 0.368 tonnes per GJ. Observed cell footprint and selected polygon area differ; neither is measured burned area. A last detection is not an official containment or extinction date.
